title: Шаги как валюта казуального пазла (реальный мир как вход)
market: Casual puzzle × Geolocation / Gyms & Fitness (Pikmin Bloom, WeWard)
claim: Casual-пазл, в котором ходы и бустеры начисляются за реальные шаги (HealthKit / Google Fit), даст удержание и выручку на установку выше контрольного варианта без шагов: спрос на «движение за награду» ускоряется (Pikmin Bloom и WeWard растут двузначно при падающем рынке игр), а механика шагов не требует карты, AR или IP.

evidence.metric: Pikmin Bloom rev_cur_best_usd / rev_yoy_best / s_rev_h2_h1 / s_rev_last3m_yoy
Gyms & Fitness top100_rev_yoy; Personal Health & Fitness rev_yoy / dl_yoy

accessibility: Сборка на существующем sort/merge-движке — высокая; барьер — у лидера IP Nintendo/Niantic и карта; WeWard монетизируется партнёрами и рекламой; пермишен HealthKit снижает конверсию в онбординге.
prototype_idea: Sort- или merge-пазл с дневным лимитом ходов, который пополняется шагами (1 000 шагов = N ходов), бустеры за 5 000/10 000 шагов, виджет шагов на экране блокировки; без карты и AR.
revenue_test: Два playable-варианта (с «шаги = ходы» и без) → фильтр креатива 7 дней (US/CA, ~$1.5K) → софт-лонч iOS CA/AU 14 дней (~$3K). Деньги: выручка на установку к D7 (IAP + реклама) против CPI; гейт — не ниже контроля по D7-выручке и +20% D7-удержания. Итого ≤ 28 дней.
risks: Ядро петли — привычка, а не расход; шаговые игры монетизируются слабо (WeWard — рекламой); рост Pikmin Bloom может быть событием/обновлением 2026, а не трендом категории; Android-фрагментация датчиков.

verification.reasoning: The headline numbers reproduce exactly from leaders.csv. Pikmin Bloom is at $49.69M against $29.93M prior (+66.0%), with h2/h1 +91.6% and last3m +114.2%. WeWard is at $10.64M against $4.37M (+143.1%, last3m +163.2%). Their sum, $60.3M against $34.3M, gives the stated size and +75% yoy. The claimed mechanism, that demand for movement-for-reward is accelerating, does not hold up beyond these two apps. It rests on two hand-picked apps, and WeWard's prior base is only $4.4M, so its growth is a small-base effect. A broader basket of walk and step products from leaders.csv falls from $216.3M to $178.0M (-17.7%). That basket is Dragon Quest Walk ($120.1M to $69.0M, -42.5%), Pikmin Bloom, Monster Hunter Now ($44.3M to $33.8M, -23.7%), WeWard, WalkFit ($10.9M to $7.1M), StepsApp, Sweatcoin ($1.59M to $1.19M) and Step Counter - Pedometer. The Geolocation sub-genre as a whole is -2.2% yoy ($818.5M to $800.2M), and Pokémon GO holds 73.5% of it. Its +35.9% last3m comes from a single July 2026 spike ($127.0M against about $50-65M in other months), likely an event; Disney Step, a 2025 new entrant, is already -42%. Pikmin's growth did not come from its home market: Japan fell from $15.04M to $12.78M in country_leaders.csv, and Korea dropped out of the current top list after $5.97M prior. So the growth is a single-title, ex-Japan story. It is probably update- or event-driven (peak month 2026-05), not a category trend. Personal Health & Fitness is +8.2% revenue, but it is slowing: last3m +2.5%, with downloads -6.3% yoy and -9.9% last3m. Gyms & Fitness top-100 growth (+9.3%) is driven by Strava, Runna and LADDER, not by step-reward apps. The contrast with a falling games market is also misleading: the Puzzle genre itself is +17.5% yoy (niche_dynamics_game_genre.csv), so the control arm sits in a growing genre. WeWard's mostly non-IAP monetization means its revenue is understated, but in the other direction Sweatcoin's IAP is shrinking even though it has 30.5M downloads. None of this data can test the actual product claim, a retention and revenue lift from steps-as-moves, so the test plan is still reasonable as an experiment, just not market-backed.

verification.key_caveat: The "movement-for-reward" growth signal comes from two hand-picked apps: Pikmin Bloom, which is shrinking in Japan, and WeWard, which grew from a $4.4M base. The wider basket of walk and step games and step-reward apps fell 17.7% yoy ($216M to $178M), and the Geolocation sub-genre is -2.2%. Treat this as an untested mechanic bet, not as following a growing category.

verification.reasoning:
The claim that demand for "movement for a reward" is accelerating rests on two apps, not on the category. In niche_leaders_full_game_sub_genre.csv the Geolocation top-100 is down 2.2% YoY ($800.2M vs $818.5M). Pokémon GO alone holds 73.5% of it (HHI 0.553), and US publishers hold 85.5% of the top-5 mix. The 52 new entrants together take 0.22% of top-100 revenue ($1.74M), which leaves almost no room for a new entrant.

Other step and walking titles fell sharply (leaders.csv): Dragon Quest Walk −$51.1M (−43%), Disney Step −42%, Monster Hunter Now −24%, Shutsujin −30%, WalkFit −34%, Sweatcoin IAP −25%. Summing the step and walking apps I checked, excluding Pokémon GO, gives −$44.8M. Pikmin Bloom (+$19.8M) and WeWard (+$6.3M) cover only part of that drop.

Pikmin Bloom's growth comes with Nintendo/Niantic IP, and its revenue peaked in 2026-05, so it may be one strong update rather than a trend. The Geolocation +35.9% last-3-months figure is mostly a single spike: July 2026 at $127.0M (niche_monthly_game_sub_genre.csv), the same month as Pokémon GO's peak, which looks like an event.

Nothing in the data shows a casual puzzle game earning more money because of a step mechanic. The mechanic also works against how puzzle games make money: giving out free moves and boosters for steps replaces the very things IAP sells.

The proposed test cannot measure money:
- The 7-day creative filter measures CTR/IPM, i.e. clicks.
- $3K of iOS soft launch in CA/AU buys roughly 750–1,200 installs, about 400–600 per arm. At the usual casual-puzzle payer rate of 1–2% by D7 (an industry assumption, not from our data), that is single-digit payers per arm, so the "not below control on D7 revenue" gate is statistical noise.
- A habit loop does not pay back by D7 anyway.

Ad revenue does not rescue the case. WeWard's real monetization (partners, offerwall, ads) is invisible in IAP, and Geolocation already has ad_intensity_us_cur = 1.58. That means more of the demand is ad-monetized, which favours scale and UA budget, not a small studio's IAP puzzle.

Platform friction adds to this:
- The HealthKit permission prompt during onboarding.
- App Store rule 5.1.3: health data must not be used for advertising.
- Google Fit APIs are being replaced by Health Connect, which splits Android support.

As a cheap feature experiment on the existing sort/merge engine it is buildable. As a business opportunity with a money-based test in 4 weeks, it does not hold up.

verification.key_caveat: The "growth in walk-for-reward demand" is two apps, one of them on Nintendo IP (Pikmin Bloom +$19.8M, WeWard +$6.3M). The Geolocation category as a whole is down 2.2% YoY, new entrants hold 0.22% of it, and other step games lost about $45M. A $3K soft launch gives single-digit payers per arm, so it cannot measure D7 revenue: this is a feature experiment, not a validated market.

title: Литургический календарь как лайвопс: квиз/пазл по стиху дня с запуском к Адвенту
claim: Категория Religion & Spirituality растёт за счёт новичков (top-100 +22.9%, 32 новых релиза с долей 23.6%, HHI 0.08), а падение H2/H1 — сезонность Великого поста (год к году за июль–сентябрь +24.5%). Игровой религиозный продукт (ежедневный квиз или пазл по чтению дня со стриком и сезонным контентом Адвент → Пост) конвертирует в подписку не хуже контентных приложений, если запущен к сезонному пику 29.11.2026.

evidence.metric: Religion & Spirituality rev_cur_usd / rev_yoy / rev_h2_h1 / rev_last3m_yoy
top100_rev_cur / top100_rev_yoy / n_new_entrants / new_entrants_share / hhi / top1
Hallow rev_cur / rev_yoy / s_rev_h2_h1; Bible Chat rev_cur / rev_yoy / s_rev_h2_h1

evidence.value: 0.10, ослаблена двумя линзами в основном за H2/H1

accessibility: Низкая концентрация и 32 новичка в top-100; барьер — доверие аудитории и объём контента; политика сторов к религиозному контенту мягкая; сезонность задаёт календарь тестов.
prototype_idea: Ежедневный квиз/пазл по чтению дня (католический и протестантский лекционарии), стрик и виджет; подписка $4.99/мес с 3-дневным триалом; контент на Адвент 2026 (29.11–24.12) готов к запуску.
revenue_test: Сборка до 20.11; трафик US iOS в первые 2 недели Адвента (~$3K, Meta + TikTok); деньги: trial → paid на $1 трафика; контроль — та же воронка в не-сезонную неделю ноября; гейт — триал ≥ 5% установок и trial→paid ≥ 30%. ≤ 28 дней.
risks: Сезонность работает в обе стороны (провал после Пасхи); лидер Hallow падает (−18.8%); Bible Chat H2/H1 −44%; AI-собеседники перехватывают часть спроса; первая волна уже ослабила похожую H29 до 0.10.

verification.reasoning:
Every headline number reproduces exactly. The Religion & Spirituality row in niche_dynamics_app_sub_category.csv shows $152.62M vs $118.64M (+28.6%), H2/H1 −11.3% and last3m +24.5%. The niche_leaders_full_app_iq_category.csv row shows top-100 $127.35M vs $103.61M (+22.9%), 32 new entrants at 23.6% share, HHI 0.080 and Hallow at 23.8%.

The mechanism is where the claim breaks. Rebuilding H2/H1 from niche_monthly_app_sub_category.csv rules out the 'it's just Lent seasonality' explanation. The same split in the prior year went the other way: Oct24–Mar25 $57.56M against Apr–Sep25 $61.07M, which is H2/H1 = +6.1%. Year over year, growth slowed from +40.5% in H1 ($80.87M vs $57.56M) to +17.5% in H2 ($71.75M vs $61.07M), and monthly YoY fell to Jul +36%, Aug +30%, Sep +10.2%. Easter moving from Apr 20, 2025 to Apr 5, 2026 explains part of the gap, but not a 40→10% slowdown.

Advent is not the seasonal peak the test is timed for. December was 8.0% of annual revenue in 2025 ($12.22M of $152.6M) and 6.8% in 2024, both below the 8.3% monthly average. November 2025 ($10.80M) fell month over month. The real peaks are January and Lent: Mar-26 $19.89M, Mar-25 $16.52M and Apr-25 $15.75M, with downloads peaking Feb-26 at 159M and Mar-25 at 171M.

'Growth from newcomers' is only half true. Per growth_decomp, incumbents contributed +$14.68M, entrants +$13.97M and exits −$4.91M, so entrants are 59% of the top-100 delta and incumbents 62%. The new names are widget and AI-chat devotional apps (Bible Path UAE, Bible Widgets Spain, Duomo Cyprus, Bible Note SG, Creed), not games or quizzes. Downloads were flat at +2.4%, and growth comes from revenue per download (RPD) rising $0.101→$0.127.

The two leaders cancel out: Bible Chat +$6.26M against Hallow −$7.03M. There is no quiz or puzzle in the Religion top-100. The direct game-form analogs in the game_sub_genre top-100 lists of niche_top_apps.csv are tiny and shrinking, about $0.36M current against about $0.56M prior across five apps. That runs against the claim that a game-shaped product converts no worse than content apps, with the caveat that these analogs are probably partly ad-monetized and so undercounted in IAP-only data.

verification.key_caveat: The niche figures reproduce, but this is not just a Lent effect: the prior year's H2/H1 was +6.1%, and YoY growth slowed from +40% to +10% by September 2026. Advent is a below-average month, and the real peaks are January and Lent. The closest game-form analogs (Bible trivia, word and colouring games) earn under $0.4M IAP in total and are shrinking, so a December test should not decide whether the product converts.

verification.reasoning: The category numbers check out: rev_cur=$152.6M (+28.6%), top-100 +22.9%, 32 new entrants with a 23.6% share, HHI 0.080, and Hallow at 23.8% of the top-100. Getting into the category is realistic for a small studio, because the entrants are app-factory teams from the UAE, Spain, Cyprus and Singapore. The idea fails on the two claims that set it apart from H29. First, games do not monetize like content apps. None of the 100 top-grossing Religion & Spirituality apps is a quiz or puzzle. The direct comparables live in the game taxonomy and earn very little from in-app purchases, and they are shrinking: Daily Bible Trivia made $72K (down from $194K), Versle earned $35K, Bible Trivia - Bible Quiz Game made $32K on 873K downloads ($0.037 per download), and Bible Word Puzzle made $176K on 5.0M downloads (-36%). The content apps the claim measures itself against earn far more per download: Hallow $4.83, Ascension $10.90, Duomo $2.24, and even the widget apps $0.70–0.78. Second, there is no Advent peak. December 2025 was $12.22M against November's $10.80M (+13%), and December 2024 was +8% over November. The real peaks are January (New Year) and March, at $19.89M in March 2026. That March peak comes from Lent/Easter and from Ramadan: downloads peaked in February 2026 at 159M and March 2025 at 171M, driven by Quran and Athan apps. The claim already blames Lent for the weak H2/H1 (-11.3%), which contradicts calling November 29 the peak. Growth is also slowing. Year-on-year growth fell from +52% (Oct–Dec 2025 vs Oct–Dec 2024) to +24.5% (Jul–Sep), and the monthly run-rate has been flat at about $11M outside the seasonal spike. Against the high Oct–Dec 2025 base, Q4 2026 year-on-year growth is likely close to zero. The revenue test does measure money: a 3-day trial converting to paid fits inside 28 days. But $3K of US iOS traffic, at an assumed $2–3 per install, buys about 1,000–1,500 installs, so about 50–75 trials and 15–22 payers. That sample cannot separate an Advent effect of about 10% from a November control. Platform policy risk is low. The real exposure is that this genre makes its money from ads (the comparables have about 1M downloads and almost no in-app revenue), so a subscription paywall goes against what the comparables show.

Religious quiz and puzzle games already exist and earn tens of thousands of dollars a year in in-app purchases, mostly from ads ($0.04 per download, against $2–11 for content apps). Advent is not the seasonal peak (December is only +8–13% over November; the peaks are January and Lent/Ramadan in March). A $3K test cannot measure a seasonal effect.

title: Бюджет-трекер как сити-билдер (модель Fortune City)
claim: Фрагментированная растущая категория (+20.5% по подкатегории, top-100 +17.5%, HHI 0.055, лидер Money Forward с 13.5%, всего 8 новичков) примет геймифицированный трекер расходов по подписке: игровая мета (город растёт от записей) даёт удержание выше обычных трекеров, а регуляторных барьеров при ручном вводе нет.

evidence.metric: Budget & Expense Tracking rev_cur_usd / rev_yoy / rev_h2_h1 / dl_yoy
top100_rev_cur / top100_rev_yoy / n_new_entrants / new_entrants_share / hhi / top1
Fortune City presence in global top-2000

accessibility: Нет глобального лидера, концентрация минимальная; банковские интеграции не нужны при ручном вводе; барьер — удержание привычки и дорогая UA в finance.
prototype_idea: Ручной ввод траты за 3 секунды → здание растёт в городе; еженедельные цели экономии как квесты; подписка $4.99/мес или $29.99/год.
revenue_test: Лендинг с реальной подпиской + TestFlight/soft launch US и DE на 2 недели (~$3K); деньги: оплаты на $1 трафика и CAC на плательщика; вторичная — записей на пользователя к D7. ≤ 28 дней.
risks: Трекеры — рынок привычки с высоким оттоком; дорогая UA в финансах; оригинальный Fortune City (2017) не вырос до top-2000; рост подкатегории может идти от японских и корейских локальных лидеров, а не от геймификации.

verification.reasoning: The headline numbers reproduce exactly. niche_dynamics_app_sub_category.csv gives Budget & Expense Tracking rev_cur=$136.35M against prior $113.17M (+20.5%), rev_h2_h1=+0.30%, last3m_yoy=+16.8% and dl_yoy=+31.3%. niche_leaders_full_app_iq_category.csv gives top100 $117.93M against $100.34M (+17.5%), HHI 0.0556, top1 Money Forward $15.97M (13.5%) and 8 new entrants. Fortune City and every other gamified tracker are missing from leaders.csv, and the only top-100 names that hint at play are not games (Zaim, and 飞鸭AI记账, an AI chat bookkeeper). The growth mechanism does not support the thesis, though. New entrants can get in, but in the opposite format to the one proposed. The small Western winners are standalone pass-the-phone word-impostor apps: Fakeit (Poland) $8.55M, Splash (Germany) $4.91M and Imposter Who? (US) $2.79M. That runs against the premise that standalone party games monetize weakly and need to sit inside a puzzle. No app in leaders.csv or niche_top_apps.csv combines a puzzle with an impostor mode. The data room also has no k-factor or retention data. So the claim that a hybrid beats a standalone party game has no evidence behind it at all.

The test cannot measure money. TestFlight in-app purchases run in the sandbox and nobody is charged, so revenue per install by D7 is zero by construction. The pass/fail gate (k ≥ 0.3 and D7 at least 20% above control) measures engagement, not revenue. The one-phone mode also creates almost no installs, because all players share one device, so k ≥ 0.3 can only come from the async link mode. That mode adds user-generated text and chat moderation, and it brings a teen/kids audience into scope.

Some of the demand is ad-monetized and invisible in IAP data. Spy Undercover has 31.6M downloads but only $1.38M in revenue, about $0.04 per download. The tag count also nearly doubled, from 2,562 to 4,941 apps, which suggests a wave of clones and raises the risk of rejection under App Store guideline 4.3 (spam and copycat apps).
